android.desc:
Poweramp plays local music files and radio streams in various formats, including Hi-Res, with powerful Bass/Treble and Equalization controls.

Features
===
• Audio engine:
  • supports hi-res output
  • custom DSP, including updated Equalizer/Tone/Stereo expand, and the Reverb/Tempo effects
  • unique DVC (Direct Volume Control) mode allowing powerful equalization/bass/tone control without distortion
  • internal 64bit processing
  • AutoEq presets
  • configurable per-output Options
  • configurable resampler, dither options
  • opus, tak, mka, dsd dsf/dff formats support
  • radios/streams in .m3u format
  • gapless smoothing

• UI:
  • visualizations (.milk presets and spectrum)
  • synchronized/plain lyrics
  • Light and Dark skins included, both with Pro Buttons and Static Seekbar options
  • as previously, 3rd party skins are available

Other features:
- multiband graphical equalizer for all supported formats, built-in and custom presets. Up to 32 bands supported
- parametric equalizer mode where each band is added and configured separately
- separate powerful Bass/Treble
- stereo eXpansion, mono mixing, balance, tempo control, reverb, system MusicFX (if supported by the device)
- Android Auto
- Chromecast
- Direct Volume Control (DVC) for extended dynamic range and really deep bass
- crossfade
- gapless 
- replay gain
- plays songs from folders and from own library
- dynamic queue
- lyrics support, including lyrics search via plugin
- embed and standalone .cue files support
- support for m3u, m3u8, pls, wpl playlists, playlist importing and exporting
- downloads missing album art
- artist images downloading
- custom visual themes, skins available on Play
- widgets with an advanced customization
- lock screen options
- Milkdrop compatible visualization support (and 3rd party downloadable visualizations)
- tag editor
- audio info with detailed audio processing information
- high level of customization via settings

* Android Auto, Chromecast are trademarks of Google LLC.

quotes.text:
I had exactly this problem when listening to music on my phone using cheap, low-impedance earbuds! I searched for audio player apps that offer some equalizer controls. One option is to lower all the sliders equally across the different frequencies, but it's easier to get an app that also has a single "preamp" slider which affects the signal across all frequencies. I settled on Poweramp [0], which has a two week free trial. I bought the full version (4 USD) after confirming that it did what I wanted.

I agree with the other answers about getting an in-line volume control -- if you're using wired headphones. They're also great on airplanes: turn the provided entertainment up to maximum volume with the buttons on the armrest or wherever; turn the volume on the in-line attenuator down to nearly zero; listen in comfort. I noticed that whenever an announcement is made in the cabin, it seems to disregard your volume setting on the entertainment and just blasts your ears at 100%. If you've already set your in-line attenuator to deal with movies at 100%, then the announcement doesn't hurt your eardrums. I bought this one because it doesn't add a lot of extra length to the cable [1].

[0] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.maxmpz.audioplayer

[1] https://www.amazon.com/dp/B008DJTB32
